name: Example: Applying the Root Rule to Compute a Limit
worked_solution:
Applying the quotient rule, we get

$$
\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 1} \dfrac{\sqrt{x+8}}{x-2}
=\dfrac{\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 1} \sqrt{x+8}}{\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 1}(x-2)}.
$$

We calculate the limits of the numerator and denominator, separately.

Applying the root rule in the numerator, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 1}\sqrt{x+8} & =\sqrt{{lim}_{x\to 1}(x+8)} \\  & =\sqrt{1+8} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

For the denominator, we have
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 1}(x-2) & =1-2 \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{\sqrt{x+8}}{x-2} & =\frac{3}{(-1)} \\  & =-3\,.\end{aligned}
$$
